runs.content: Yum China (YUMC) picked up at the previous close ($47.72) — Morningstar flags it 40% undervalued (FV $77), reinforced by a Q2 beat-and-raise (EPS $0.70 vs $0.67 est, revenue +13% YoY) and a fresh multi-analyst buy wave (Citic, Nomura, Jefferies, UOB Kay Hian, Huatai, Guotai Haitong), chosen over CLX (post-earnings double analyst downgrade, PTs below spot) and CPB (deepest discount but structurally challenged category). CMCL hit T1 (+25.50% @ $21.75) and RDW hit T2 (+60.45% @ $13.59) — both mechanical tranche sales, positions remain open. RIVN and MRNA recovered off WATCH; JBHT remains WATCH (−10.02%), no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,851 (+3.78% on $49,000).

Lithia Motors (LAD) picked up at the previous close ($375.78) — a still-early 3-month momentum setup (+29.0%, RSI 58.8) reinforced by a Q2 EPS beat and a cheap ~12.5x P/E, chosen as market leadership broadens away from the narrow AI-megacap trade (Dow record close vs. Nasdaq −0.8% on weak AI names). FICO was stopped out today at $1,031.89 (−15.93%, −$159.25) after a Wolfe Research downgrade on VantageScore competitive-pressure concerns breached the −15% stop. RIVN (−10.48%) and JBHT (−10.44%) both crossed the −10% signal-assessment threshold but were held — neither carries a Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,154 (+2.40% on $48,000).
